messages:
Noah (PM): Starting thread for a new packaging idea: 'Dynamic Route Throttle Credits' (DRT). The gist: customers pre-buy credits that can be spent to temporarily increase route concurrency or enable a short burst allowance for specific routes instead of paying for reserved capacity. Need input on scope, pricing shapes, and launch gates.

Ava (Eng): Implementation sketch: credit-check at ingress; if credits available apply a per-request concurrency token that allows bypassing a route-level limiter (for N requests or T seconds). Two modes: burst-concurrency (more simultaneous requests) or sustained-burst (higher qps for short window). Need very cheap lookup, metrics tagging, and safety rails to avoid overload.

Leo (DevEx): Console UX: attach DRT to a route, pick mode (burst | sustained), set budget and auto-apply triggers (deploys, campaign start), and surface predicted request coverage. Also show per-customer historical burn and an alert if top-ups low. Pilot UI can be minimal CLI + Console toggle.

Marta (Sales): Customers asking for something like this — they want predictable, on-demand headroom without committing to monthly reserved pools. Pilot pitch: "on-demand concurrency credits for critical endpoints". Pricing thought: bundle and PAYG; offer pilot credit grants.

Ishaan (Finance): Need mapping: 1 credit = X allowed extra concurrent request-seconds or Y additional requests at peak. Margin depends on whether extra concurrency forces more reserved GPUs. For soft-mode (no hard reserve) markup can be high; for hard-mode (reserved slots) treat like Dedicated seat. Watch revenue recognition for prepaid bundles.

Rina (Legal): Touchpoints: avoid SLO wording unless it's a reserved SKU. For soft DRT: advertise "probabilistic priority" or "burst allowance". If customers want guaranteed concurrency we must create a reserved SKU with clear SLA and associated penalties. Also include abuse clause and a rollback/kill-switch in T&Cs.

Noah (PM): Proposed pilot scope: soft-mode DRT only (no hard-reserve), route-level attach, two pilot customers, Console + API, and billing telemetry. Launch gates: clear latency improvement for targeted routes, platform cost increase <6% at 99th, and no security/legal blockers.

Ava (Eng): Effort estimate: spec + design ~1 week, routing hooks + cheap token store ~2 sprints, Console hooks ~1 sprint. Must include: global kill-switch, backpressure propagation, and a guard that drains credits before impacting unrelated routes.

Leo (DevEx): Example CLI/API snippet for pilots I'll mock:

```
# attach 500 credits to /v1/search for 72h in burst mode
redwood routes attach-credits --route /v1/search --sku DRT-500 --mode burst --duration 72h --auto-apply deploys
```

Marta (Sales): Example SKU ideas for discussion: DRT-500 (500 credits) $199/30d, DRT-2K (2000 credits) $699/30d, PAYG $0.45/credit. Pilot offer: 500 free credits for 60 days. We'll adjust after sims.

Ishaan (Finance): Quick simulation ask: what is the delta cost if a route consumes 500 credits during a 3-minute spike vs baseline? Need conservative margin assumptions. Also, define refund/rollover policy for unused credits.

Rina (Legal): Add pilot clause: no implied SLA; provider can revoke DRT if platform health degrades. For enterprise pilot we can offer a reserved DRT with an SLA in exchange for commitment and different pricing. I'll draft T&Cs.

Ava (Eng): Ops ask: run two sims: (1) 3min 10x spike with 40% requests eligible for DRT; (2) steady 30min medium uplift. Capture credit burn, tail latency improvement, and cluster CPU/GPU delta. @ops-bot can you schedule?

ops-bot: Scheduled simulations: job #12011 (3min 10x spike) and job #12012 (30min steady uplift). ETA ~2h. Results will be posted to this thread.

Noah (PM): Next steps: Ava -> tech spec + safety-mode; Leo -> Console mock + CLI examples; Rina -> pilot T&Cs; Marta -> shortlist pilot customers; Ishaan -> refine pricing & margin model. I'll draft PRD and success metrics by EOD Friday. Thanks! :sparkles:
